```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import tables as T          # complex tables: merged cells, footnotes (T.<builder>(...).show())
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as sstat
import re
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

DOC = "PCR-010"
UO = "ufdf"
UO_TITLE = "Ultrafiltration / Diafiltration (Step 10)"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ formatting
def mn(s):
    """A formatted number with a true minus sign, and no sign on a value that rounds to zero."""
    s = str(s)
    if s.startswith("-"):
        return ("−" + s[1:]) if any(ch in "123456789" for ch in s) else s[1:]
    return s

def fx(x, d=2):
    return mn(f"{float(x):,.{d}f}")

def fg(x):
    return mn(f"{float(x):g}")

def pv(p):
    return "< 0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"{p:.3f}"

def pe(p):
    return "p < 0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"p = {p:.3f}"

WORDS = {1: "one", 2: "two", 3: "three", 4: "four", 5: "five", 6: "six", 7: "seven",
         8: "eight", 9: "nine", 10: "ten", 11: "eleven", 12: "twelve"}

def w(n):
    return WORDS.get(int(n), f"{int(n)}")

def Cap(s):
    return s[:1].upper() + s[1:]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ parameters (config)
uo = CFG.unit_op(UO)
STEP_N = uo.step
PK = [p.key for p in uo.parameters]
assert PK == ["diavolumes", "tmp", "final_conc"]
PRM = {k: uo.param(k) for k in PK}
NAME = {k: PRM[k].name for k in PK}                          # as the config names it
nm = {k: NAME[k][0].lower() + NAME[k][1:] for k in PK}       # inside a sentence
UNIT = {k: PRM[k].unit for k in PK}
SP = {k: float(PRM[k].setpoint) for k in PK}
NOR = {k: tuple(map(float, PRM[k].nor)) for k in PK}
RNG = {k: tuple(map(float, PRM[k].prange)) for k in PK}
CLS = {k: PRM[k].classification for k in PK}
N_P = len(PK)
for k in PK:
    # the NOR and set-point in force are those the studies were planned against
    assert tuple(map(float, PRM[k].nor_characterized)) == NOR[k]
    assert PRM[k].setpoint_characterized is None or float(PRM[k].setpoint_characterized) == SP[k]
    assert RNG[k][0] <= NOR[k][0] <= SP[k] <= NOR[k][1] <= RNG[k][1]
assert set(CLS.values()) == {"KPP"}                         # every parameter of the step is a KPP
EXT_LOW = {k: RNG[k][0] < NOR[k][0] for k in PK}
EXT_HIGH = {k: RNG[k][1] > NOR[k][1] for k in PK}
assert EXT_LOW == {"diavolumes": False, "tmp": False, "final_conc": True} and all(EXT_HIGH.values())

def u_(k, v):
    return f"{fg(v)} {UNIT[k]}"

def rng_s(k):
    return f"{fg(RNG[k][0])}–{fg(RNG[k][1])} {UNIT[k]}"

def nor_s(k):
    return f"{fg(NOR[k][0])}–{fg(NOR[k][1])} {UNIT[k]}"

def sp_s(k):
    return u_(k, SP[k])

DS_TARGET = float(CFG.raw()["meta"]["drug_substance_target_g_per_l"])
assert DS_TARGET == SP["final_conc"]
SCALE_L = f"{int(V['commercial_scale_l']):,}"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ studies, equipment, registers
CHR = csv("study_chronology.csv")
CHR = CHR[CHR["step"] == UO].set_index("id")
SDM_ID, UNI_ID, UNI2_ID = "S-UFDF-SDM", "S-UFDF-UNI", "S-UFDF-UNI2"
assert set(CHR.index) == {SDM_ID, UNI_ID, UNI2_ID}
SDM_START, SDM_END, SDM_EQ = CHR.loc[SDM_ID, ["start", "end", "equipment"]]
UNI_START, UNI_END, UNI_EQ = CHR.loc[UNI_ID, ["start", "end", "equipment"]]
UNI2_START, UNI2_END, UNI2_EQ = CHR.loc[UNI2_ID, ["start", "end", "equipment"]]
EQT = equipment_df().set_index("Equipment")
CALDUE = {e: EQT.loc[e, "Next calibration due"] for e in {SDM_EQ, UNI_EQ, UNI2_EQ}}
assert all(EQT.loc[e, "Calibration status"] == "in calibration at execution" for e in CALDUE)
assert SDM_EQ == UNI_EQ != UNI2_EQ
assert SDM_END < UNI_START                     # the offset runs were complete before characterization
for _s in CHR.index:
    assert CHR.loc[_s, "end"] < CALDUE[CHR.loc[_s, "equipment"]]
assert UNI2_START > INV["closed"] and UNI2_END < EFFECTIVE_DATE and UNI_END < REV1["effective"]

PDS = PLAN_DISCREPANCIES[DOC]
assert len(PDS) == 1 and PDS[0]["studies"] == [UNI2_ID]
PD1 = PDS[0]["id"]
EVS = dev_facts(DOC)
assert list(EVS["dev_id"]) == ["DEV-010-01", "DEV-010-02"] and (EVS["disposition"] == "retained").all()
EV1_EQ = EVS.loc[0, "equipment"]
EV2_METHOD = EVS.loc[1, "method"]
assert EV1_EQ == SDM_EQ and pd.isna(EVS.loc[1, "equipment"]) and EV2_METHOD == "AMV-3019"
assert NOR["tmp"][1] < dev_010_01_tmp_max_psi <= RNG["tmp"][1]
assert not ({"study", "run"} & set(EVS.columns))      # the event record names no study and no run
_cex = D.iac_limit("cex", "aggregate_out_pct")
assert _cex[2] == "upper" and _cex[1] == D.effective_acceptance(UO, "aggregate_out_pct")[1]
assert D.acceptance_basis("cex", "aggregate_out_pct") == "drug substance"
assert NOR["final_conc"][0] <= dev_010_02_conc_pre_g_per_l < SP["final_conc"]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the univariate study
UNIALL = csv("univariate_studies.csv")
assert set(UNIALL.loc[UNIALL["step"] == UO, "study"]) == {UNI2_ID}   # S-UFDF-UNI has no recorded result
U = UNIALL[UNIALL["study"] == UNI2_ID].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
LEVELS = ["low", "low-mid", "set-point", "mid-high", "high"]
assert set(U["level"]) == set(LEVELS)
N_LEV = len(LEVELS)
_cnt = U.groupby(["parameter", "value"]).size()
N_REP = int(U["replicate"].max())
assert N_REP == 2 and (_cnt == N_REP).all() and len(_cnt) == N_LEV * N_P
N_RUNS2 = len(U)
N_SER = N_LEV * N_REP
N_SP2 = int((U["level"] == "set-point").sum())
for k in PK:
    _lv = U[U["parameter"] == k].groupby("level")["value"].first()
    assert (_lv["low"], _lv["high"], _lv["set-point"]) == (RNG[k][0], RNG[k][1], SP[k])
    assert np.isclose(_lv["low-mid"], (_lv["low"] + _lv["set-point"]) / 2)
    assert np.isclose(_lv["mid-high"], (_lv["set-point"] + _lv["high"]) / 2)
U["yield_pct"] = 100 * U["step_yield"]
_held = {c for c in UNIALL.columns[6:] if U[c].notna().all()}
assert _held == {"acidic_variants", "step_yield", "aggregate_out_pct", "residual_buffer_pct",
                 "ds_concentration_g_per_l"}
# the record holds no pH, conductivity series, load, permeate, duration or run-order result
assert not [c for c in U.columns if re.search(r"(^|_)ph($|_)", c) or "conduct" in c or "order" in c
            or "permeate" in c or "duration" in c or "pool_id" in c]
assert U[[c for c in U.columns if "load" in c]].isna().all().all()

RESP = ["aggregate_out_pct", "acidic_variants", "residual_buffer_pct", "yield_pct", "ds_concentration_g_per_l"]
RLAB = {"aggregate_out_pct": "Aggregates, HMW (%)", "acidic_variants": "Acidic variants (%)",
        "residual_buffer_pct": "Residual process buffer (%)", "yield_pct": "Step yield (%)",
        "ds_concentration_g_per_l": "Final concentration (g/L)"}
RDEC = {"aggregate_out_pct": 2, "acidic_variants": 1, "residual_buffer_pct": 4, "yield_pct": 1,
        "ds_concentration_g_per_l": 1}
ALPHA = float(THRESHOLDS["effect_alpha"])
AG, AC = "aggregate_out_pct", "acidic_variants"

def fit_line(k, r):
    g = U[U["parameter"] == k]
    lr = sstat.linregress(g["value"], g[r])
    t = sstat.t.ppf(0.975, len(g) - 2)
    wd = RNG[k][1] - RNG[k][0]
    return dict(slope=lr.slope, ic=lr.intercept, se=lr.stderr, p=lr.pvalue,
                lo=lr.slope - t * lr.stderr, hi=lr.slope + t * lr.stderr, n=len(g), dfr=len(g) - 2,
                width=wd, ch=lr.slope * wd, ch_lo=(lr.slope - t * lr.stderr) * wd,
                ch_hi=(lr.slope + t * lr.stderr) * wd)

SL = {(k, r): fit_line(k, r) for k in PK for r in RESP}
SIG = {kr for kr, v in SL.items() if v["p"] < ALPHA}
assert SIG == {("diavolumes", "residual_buffer_pct"), ("tmp", AG), ("final_conc", AG),
               ("final_conc", "ds_concentration_g_per_l")}
N_SIG, N_SLOPES = len(SIG), len(SL)
SLDF = SL[("diavolumes", AG)]["dfr"]
sC, sT, sDV = SL[("final_conc", AG)], SL[("tmp", AG)], SL[("diavolumes", AG)]
assert sC["lo"] > 0 and sT["lo"] > 0 and sC["ch"] > sT["ch"]
CH_C_NOR = sC["slope"] * (NOR["final_conc"][1] - NOR["final_conc"][0])
CH_T_NOR = sT["slope"] * (NOR["tmp"][1] - NOR["tmp"][0])
# no slope of an attribute other than these two, and none of the step yield
assert not any((k, AC) in SIG for k in PK) and not any((k, "yield_pct") in SIG for k in PK)

def pooled_sd(r):
    grp = U.groupby(["parameter", "value"])[r]
    ss = float(((U[r] - grp.transform("mean")) ** 2).sum())
    dfp = len(U) - grp.ngroups
    return float(np.sqrt(ss / dfp)), int(dfp)

PE = {r: pooled_sd(r) for r in RESP}
PE_DF = PE[AG][1]
# PCP-010 §5.3: the rule for small changes and the slope test agree for aggregate, for every parameter
for k in PK:
    _s = SL[(k, AG)]
    assert (abs(_s["ch"]) > PE[AG][0]) == (_s["p"] < ALPHA)
MET = csv("dev_methods.csv").set_index("id")
ICIEF_LOQ = float(MET.loc["AMV-3013", "loq"])
A280_PREC = float(MET.loc["AMV-3019", "precision_pct"])
assert U[AC].min() > 10 * ICIEF_LOQ
AC_MEAN = float(U[AC].mean())

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ criteria and offsets
ACC_AG = D.effective_acceptance(UO, AG)
ACC_AC = D.effective_acceptance(UO, AC)
assert ACC_AG[2] == "upper" and ACC_AC[2] == "two_sided"
AG_HI = float(ACC_AG[1])
AC_LO, AC_HI = float(ACC_AC[0]), float(ACC_AC[1])
assert D.iac_table(UO).empty and D.rev1_criteria(UO).empty
assert D.acceptance_basis(UO, AG) == D.acceptance_basis(UO, AC) == "drug substance"
CRIT_AG = f"≤ {fg(AG_HI)} % HMW"
CRIT_AC = f"{fg(AC_LO)}–{fg(AC_HI)} %"
SDM_OUT = ["step_yield", AG, "ds_concentration_g_per_l", "flux_lmh"]
OFF = {r: D.sdm_offset(UO, r) for r in SDM_OUT}
assert all(o is not None and o["scale"] == "difference" for o in OFF.values())
assert all(o["lo"] < 0 < o["hi"] for o in OFF.values())              # every interval includes zero
assert OFF[AG]["offset"] > 0 and OFF["step_yield"]["offset"] < 0     # the direction the hold-up predicts
assert D.sdm_offset(UO, AC) is None and D.sdm_offset(UO, "residual_buffer_pct") is None
N_SD, N_M = OFF[AG]["n_sd"], OFF[AG]["n_m"]
assert all((o["n_sd"], o["n_m"]) == (N_SD, N_M) for o in OFF.values())
OFF_CI = int(round(100 * OFF[AG]["ci"]))
assert not T.sdm_offsets_data([UO])["judged"].any()

U["agg_mfg"] = D.to_mfg(UO, AG, U[AG].to_numpy(float))
with D.offset_at("lo"):
    AGG_AT_LO = np.asarray(D.to_mfg(UO, AG, U[AG].to_numpy(float)))
with D.offset_at("hi"):
    AGG_AT_HI = np.asarray(D.to_mfg(UO, AG, U[AG].to_numpy(float)))
U["in_nor"] = [NOR[k][0] <= v <= NOR[k][1] for k, v in zip(U["parameter"], U["value"])]
_inn = U["in_nor"].to_numpy()
Q_AG = {"point": bool((U.loc[U["in_nor"], "agg_mfg"] <= AG_HI).all()),
        "lo": bool((AGG_AT_LO[_inn] <= AG_HI).all()), "hi": bool((AGG_AT_HI[_inn] <= AG_HI).all())}
QUAL_AG = len(set(Q_AG.values())) == 1
assert QUAL_AG and Q_AG["point"]
N_IN_NOR = int(_inn.sum())
AGG_NOR_WORST = float(max(AGG_AT_LO[_inn].max(), AGG_AT_HI[_inn].max(), U.loc[U["in_nor"], "agg_mfg"].max()))

SP2 = U[U["level"] == "set-point"]
AGG_SP2_MEAN = float(SP2[AG].mean())
AGG_SDM_MEAN, AGG_MFG_MEAN = OFF[AG]["mean_sd"], OFF[AG]["mean_m"]

AC_MET = bool(U[AC].between(AC_LO, AC_HI).all())
AG_MET = bool((U["agg_mfg"] <= AG_HI).all())
AG_MET_ENDS = bool((AGG_AT_LO <= AG_HI).all() and (AGG_AT_HI <= AG_HI).all())
assert AC_MET and AG_MET and AG_MET_ENDS
_i = U["agg_mfg"].idxmax()
AGG_MAX, AGG_MAX_K, AGG_MAX_V = float(U.loc[_i, "agg_mfg"]), U.loc[_i, "parameter"], float(U.loc[_i, "value"])
AGG_MARGIN = AG_HI - AGG_MAX
_i = U[AC].idxmin()
AC_MIN, AC_MIN_K, AC_MIN_V = float(U.loc[_i, AC]), U.loc[_i, "parameter"], float(U.loc[_i, "value"])
_i = U[AC].idxmax()
AC_MAX, AC_MAX_K, AC_MAX_V = float(U.loc[_i, AC]), U.loc[_i, "parameter"], float(U.loc[_i, "value"])
AC_MARGIN_LO, AC_MARGIN_HI = AC_MIN - AC_LO, AC_HI - AC_MAX
AC_CH_BOUND = max(max(abs(SL[(k, AC)]["ch_lo"]), abs(SL[(k, AC)]["ch_hi"])) for k in PK)
SHARE_C = 100 * sC["ch"] / AGG_MARGIN               # the larger aggregate change, against the margin
AC_CH_MAX_K = max(PK, key=lambda k: abs(SL[(k, AC)]["ch"]))
AC_CH_MAX = SL[(AC_CH_MAX_K, AC)]["ch"]
assert abs(AC_CH_MAX) > sC["ch"] and abs(AC_CH_MAX) < AC_MARGIN_LO
SHARE_C_CRIT = 100 * sC["ch"] / AG_HI

def where(k, v):
    if v == SP[k]:
        return f"at the set-point condition of the {nm[k]} series"
    return f"at {u_(k, v)} in the {nm[k]} series"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ PARs, edges, interaction bound
PARS = {}
for k in PK:
    g = U[U["parameter"] == k]
    ok = {v: bool((h["agg_mfg"] <= AG_HI).all() and h[AC].between(AC_LO, AC_HI).all())
          for v, h in g.groupby("value")}
    vals = sorted(ok)
    i0 = vals.index(SP[k])
    assert ok[vals[i0]]
    a = i0
    while a > 0 and ok[vals[a - 1]]:
        a -= 1
    b = i0
    while b < len(vals) - 1 and ok[vals[b + 1]]:
        b += 1
    PARS[k] = (vals[a], vals[b])
assert all(PARS[k] == RNG[k] for k in PK)            # every PAR reaches both edges of the range studied
MARG = {k: (NOR[k][0] - PARS[k][0], PARS[k][1] - NOR[k][1]) for k in PK}
EDGE = U[U["level"].isin(["low", "high"])]
EDGE_AG_MARGIN = float(AG_HI - EDGE["agg_mfg"].max())
EDGE_AC_MARGIN = float(min(EDGE[AC].min() - AC_LO, AC_HI - EDGE[AC].max()))
SP_AGG_MFG = float(U.loc[U["level"] == "set-point", "agg_mfg"].mean())
ADD_NOR = sC["slope"] * (NOR["final_conc"][1] - SP["final_conc"]) + sT["slope"] * (NOR["tmp"][1] - SP["tmp"])
ADD_RNG = sC["slope"] * (RNG["final_conc"][1] - SP["final_conc"]) + sT["slope"] * (RNG["tmp"][1] - SP["tmp"])
PRED_RNG = SP_AGG_MFG + ADD_RNG
GAP_RNG = AG_HI - PRED_RNG
RATIO_RNG = GAP_RNG / ADD_RNG
assert ADD_NOR > 0 and GAP_RNG > 0

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ buffer exchange
G = U[U["parameter"] == "diavolumes"]
_lrb = sstat.linregress(G["value"], np.log(G["residual_buffer_pct"]))
_tb = sstat.t.ppf(0.975, len(G) - 2)
RB_B, RB_IC = _lrb.slope, _lrb.intercept
RB_LO, RB_HI = RB_B - _tb * _lrb.stderr, RB_B + _tb * _lrb.stderr
RB_R2 = _lrb.rvalue ** 2
assert RB_LO < -1 < RB_HI                            # consistent with exp(-DV)
RB_FOLD = float(np.exp(-RB_B))
RB_REMOVED = 100 * (1 - np.exp(RB_B))
RB = G.groupby("value")["residual_buffer_pct"].agg(["min", "max", "mean"])
_dvs = list(RB.index)
assert all(RB.loc[a_, "min"] > RB.loc[b_, "max"] for a_, b_ in zip(_dvs[:-1], _dvs[1:]))   # no plateau
RB_NORLO, RB_SP, RB_TOP = RB.loc[NOR["diavolumes"][0]], RB.loc[SP["diavolumes"]], RB.loc[RNG["diavolumes"][1]]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ step yield and final concentration
Y_MEAN, Y_MIN, Y_MAX = U["yield_pct"].mean(), U["yield_pct"].min(), U["yield_pct"].max()
FC = U[U["parameter"] == "final_conc"]
FC_DIFF_MAX = float((FC["ds_concentration_g_per_l"] - FC["value"]).abs().max())
FC_OTH = U.loc[U["parameter"] != "final_conc", "ds_concentration_g_per_l"]
assert FC_OTH.between(*NOR["final_conc"]).all()
sFC = SL[("final_conc", "ds_concentration_g_per_l")]
A280_SD_AT_TARGET = A280_PREC / 100 * DS_TARGET

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ study events
DEV1_EFFECT_HI = sT["hi"] * (dev_010_01_tmp_max_psi - SP["tmp"])     # upper 95 % limit of the slope
DEV1_SHIFT = DEV1_EFFECT_HI / N_SD
assert AGG_NOR_WORST + DEV1_SHIFT <= AG_HI

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ capability (integrated model)
CAPT = cap.set_index("key")
POOS = D.p_oos().set_index("key")
MC = csv("monte_carlo.csv")
N_MC = int(V["n_monte_carlo"])
assert len(MC) == N_MC and (CAPT.loc[["aggregates_hmw", "acidic_variants", "residual_dna"], "n"] == N_MC).all()
CPK_AG = float(CAPT.loc["aggregates_hmw", "Cpk"])
CPK_AC = float(CAPT.loc["acidic_variants", "Cpk"])
CPK_DNA = float(CAPT.loc["residual_dna", "Cpk"])
assert CPK_AG >= CPK_TARGET and CPK_DNA >= CPK_TARGET and CPK_MIN <= CPK_AC < CPK_TARGET
assert CAPT.loc["acidic_variants", "Cpl"] < CAPT.loc["acidic_variants", "Cpu"]    # the lower end limits it
assert CPK_AC < min(CPK_AG, CPK_DNA)
assert CAPT.loc["residual_dna", "unit"] == "ng/dose"
NOOS = {k: int(POOS.loc[k, "n_oos"]) for k in ["aggregates_hmw", "acidic_variants", "residual_dna"]}
assert NOOS["aggregates_hmw"] == 0 and NOOS["residual_dna"] == 0 and NOOS["acidic_variants"] >= 1
PPM = {k: float(POOS.loc[k, "ppm_normal"]) for k in NOOS}
MCS = {k: (float(MC[k].mean()), float(MC[k].std(ddof=1))) for k in NOOS}
for k in NOOS:
    assert abs(MCS[k][0] - float(CAPT.loc[k, "mean"])) < 1e-3
DNA_CRIT = float(CAPT.loc["residual_dna", "acc_high"])
DNA_MEAN = MCS["residual_dna"][0]
DNA_PG = DNA_MEAN * 1000.0 / DOSE_MG
assert np.isclose(dna_ng_per_dose(DNA_PG), DNA_MEAN)
N_MC_S = f"{N_MC:,}"
P_UB_PCT = 100 * (1 - 0.05 ** (1 / N_MC))     # one-sided 95 % bound, no batch outside in N_MC

def verdict(c):
    if c >= CPK_TARGET:
        return "At or above the target"
    return "Between the minimum and the target" if c >= CPK_MIN else "Below the minimum"
```

# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

Ultrafiltration and diafiltration (UF/DF) is Step `{python} STEP_N`, the last step of the A-Mab drug substance process. It concentrates the antibody, exchanges the process buffer for the formulation buffer and delivers the drug substance at its target concentration of `{python} sp_s("final_conc")`. This report gives the results of the characterization of the step under the plan PCP-010 and the master plan PCMP-001. It is part of the Stage 1 record that supports the transfer of the process from the development site in `{python} SENDING_LOCATION` to the commercial drug substance site in `{python} RECEIVING_LOCATION`.

The step has no designed experiment. The risk assessment RA-001 assigned its `{python} w(N_P)` parameters, the `{python} nm["diavolumes"]`, the `{python} nm["tmp"]` (TMP) and the `{python} nm["final_conc"]`, to univariate study. Version 1.0 of this report described the univariate study `{python} UNI_ID` without a result for any parameter effect. The results reported here come from a further univariate study, `{python} UNI2_ID`, made from `{python} UNI2_START` to `{python} UNI2_END` on the second tangential flow filtration (TFF) skid `{python} UNI2_EQ`, after the QA investigation INV-001 had closed. Each parameter was run at `{python} w(N_LEV)` levels across its range studied, in duplicate, with the other parameters at their set-points. The study is recorded as the discrepancy `{python} PD1` from the plan. The scale-down model was qualified for aggregate by its offset from manufacturing scale, measured in the study `{python} SDM_ID`.

Every result met the drug substance criteria for aggregate (`{python} CRIT_AG`) and for the acidic charge variants (`{python} CRIT_AC`), at every level of every parameter. The proven acceptable range (PAR) of each parameter is therefore its range studied, `{python} rng_s("diavolumes")`, `{python} rng_s("tmp")` and `{python} rng_s("final_conc")`. Aggregate in the final retentate rose with the final DS concentration (`{python} pe(sC["p"])`) and with TMP (`{python} pe(sT["p"])`). Across the ranges studied the two effects amount to `{python} fx(sC["ch"])` and `{python} fx(sT["ch"])` percentage points, and the highest result lay `{python} fx(AGG_MARGIN)` percentage points below the criterion. The A-Mab case study gives nothing for this step, so the effect is a finding of this campaign. No effect of the number of diavolumes on aggregate was detected, and no slope of the acidic charge variants was significant.

The residual process buffer fell by a factor of `{python} fx(RB_FOLD)` for each diavolume, which is the fall expected when the buffer species pass the membrane freely. It still fell measurably between the last two levels of the range studied. The buffer-exchange criterion of PCP-010, a plateau of the formulation buffer at or below `{python} u_("diavolumes", NOR["diavolumes"][0])`, is therefore not met, and the record holds no pH reading for it. At `{python} u_("diavolumes", NOR["diavolumes"][0])` the residual process buffer was at most `{python} fx(RB_NORLO["max"], 3)` % of the process buffer.

All `{python} w(N_P)` parameters were classified as key process parameters (KPPs), and the step has no critical process parameter. In the integrated process model of `{python} N_MC_S` simulated batches the drug substance has a Cpk of `{python} fx(CPK_AG, 1)` for aggregate, `{python} fx(CPK_AC)` for the acidic charge variants and `{python} fx(CPK_DNA, 1)` for residual DNA, which is judged in ng per dose. The Cpk of the acidic charge variants lies between the minimum of `{python} fx(CPK_MIN)` and the target of `{python} fx(CPK_TARGET)` set by PCMP-001. It is limited by the lower end of the criterion, which this step does not drive. Version 1.0 recorded two study events, a TMP excursion to `{python} u_("tmp", dev_010_01_tmp_max_psi)` (DEV-010-01) and a final concentration of `{python} u_("final_conc", dev_010_02_conc_pre_g_per_l)` before a top-up (DEV-010-02). Neither changes a conclusion. The ranges and classes of this report roll up into the master report PCMR-001.

# Introduction {#sec-intro}

## Product and unit operation {#sec-product}

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody [@amab2009]. Its drug substance is purified by the platform train of Protein A capture, low-pH viral inactivation, cation exchange, anion exchange, small virus retentive filtration and UF/DF. UF/DF is the last step of the train, and its product is the drug substance. The commercial process runs at a production bioreactor working volume of `{python} SCALE_L` L.

The step works across a tangential flow membrane whose pores pass buffer salts and retain the antibody. Ultrafiltration removes permeate and raises the antibody concentration in the retentate. Diafiltration then adds formulation buffer at the rate at which permeate leaves, so that the retentate volume stays constant while the permeable species are washed out. A second concentration brings the retentate to the drug substance target, and a buffer flush recovers it. The step is operated under SOP-2013.

The step is not expected to change the glycan variants of A-Mab, and it is credited with no clearance of host cell protein, DNA or leached Protein A. No viral clearance is claimed for it. It can add to aggregate, which can form at the membrane wall and in the recirculation pump. It can also add to the acidic charge variants, because deamidation continues while the antibody is in solution on the skid (@sec-prior). Aggregate and the acidic charge variants are therefore the attributes measured across the step. The residual process buffer, the step yield and the final concentration are measures of process performance.

@tbl-related lists the documents to which this report is related. The paired plan is PCP-010, and the parameters were assigned to their studies by the risk assessment RA-001.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(related_docs_md(DOC))
print()
print(": Documents related to this report. {#tbl-related}")
```

## Objectives {#sec-objectives}

PCP-010 set the studies the following objectives.

(i) To estimate the offsets of a bench-scale TFF model of the commercial skid from manufacturing scale, as the basis of its qualification (PCMP-001 §7.1).
(ii) To determine the effect of the `{python} nm["diavolumes"]`, the TMP and the `{python} nm["final_conc"]` on aggregate and on the acidic charge variants of the drug substance, over the ranges studied.
(iii) To establish the number of diavolumes at which the retentate reaches the formulation buffer, so that the lower edge of the operating range rests on data for A-Mab and not on platform practice alone.
(iv) To establish a PAR for each parameter against the drug substance criteria for aggregate and the acidic charge variants.
(v) To provide the evidence on which the parameters are classified under SOP-4001, and to carry that classification into the control strategy through this report and the master report PCMR-001.

@sec-conclusions states the outcome of each objective.

## Regulatory and scientific basis {#sec-basis}

The study follows the lifecycle approach to process validation, and this report is part of the record of Stage 1, process design [@fda2011]. Development follows the enhanced approach of ICH Q8(R2) and ICH Q11, with criticality treated as a continuum and risk managed under ICH Q9 [@ichq8; @ichq11; @ichq9]. The criticality of the attributes and the logic of parameter classification come from the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]. The case study leaves UF/DF out of its characterization [@amab2009, p. 86], so it gives no expectation and no result for this step. Viral safety rests on the modular and orthogonal clearance of low-pH viral inactivation, anion exchange and small virus retentive filtration [@ichq5a]. This step contributes no log reduction to it, and the cumulative claim is consolidated in PCMR-001.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis {#sec-prior-basis}

## Platform and prior-product knowledge {#sec-prior}

The step belongs to the platform train that was used for X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab (PCMP-001 §2). The places where aggregate can form in the step are the same for every antibody, so that experience applies to the qualitative behaviour of the step. How readily an antibody aggregates depends on its colloidal stability and its self-association, which differ between antibodies. The viscosity of the retentate rises with concentration and differs between antibodies too. For this reason the final DS concentration was studied for A-Mab and was not carried over from the platform. The A-Mab case study leaves the step out [@amab2009, p. 86]. The expectations below therefore come from general knowledge of the tangential flow filtration of antibodies, as PCP-010 §4.1 records them.

Each diavolume removes a fixed fraction of the permeable species that remain in the retentate. The residual process buffer was therefore expected to fall exponentially with the number of diavolumes. At high antibody concentration, Donnan and volume-exclusion effects can leave the pH and the excipient levels of the retentate off the values of the buffer.

The membrane retains the antibody, so the antibody accumulates at the membrane wall in a polarization layer, where its concentration is higher than in the bulk retentate. The retentate also passes many times through the recirculation pump. Aggregate can form at the wall, where the antibody is most concentrated, and in the pump, where cavitation, air-liquid interfaces and particles shed by the pump can start it. Shear alone causes little aggregation of an antibody. Aggregate was therefore expected to rise with the final DS concentration, which raises the concentration in the bulk and at the wall. It was expected to rise with TMP, which below the flux limit drives more permeate and raises the concentration at the wall, and above that limit compacts the layer. It was also expected to rise with the number of passes through the pump, which more diavolumes increase. Within the normal operating ranges (NORs) the exposure is short, and the effects were expected to be small.

Deamidation of asparagine residues continues while the antibody is in solution and raises the acidic charge variants. The increase grows with the time in solution, at a rate that rises with pH and temperature. The operation lasts longer with more diavolumes, with a higher final concentration, which lowers the flux, and with a lower TMP below the flux limit. The acidic charge variants were therefore expected to rise, if at all, with the number of diavolumes and the final DS concentration, and to fall with TMP.

The effect of the final DS concentration and of TMP on aggregate that @sec-aggregate reports is a finding of this campaign. No source gave its size in advance.

## Quality attributes in scope {#sec-cqas}

@tbl-cqas lists the attributes in scope at this step, with their drug substance criteria and the criticality assigned with Tool #1 of the A-Mab case study, the product of impact and uncertainty [@amab2009]. The studies measured aggregate and the acidic charge variants in the final retentate. Both arrive with the load, and both are formed first in the production bioreactor. Deamidation continues wherever the antibody is held in solution, aggregate also forms at the low-pH elution and hold, and the cation exchange step reduces aggregate (PCMP-001 §3 and Table 7.1). Residual DNA is in scope as an attribute of the drug substance that this step delivers. It is not measured across the step and has no intermediate criterion, so it is judged on the drug substance in the integrated process model (PCMP-001 §7.3, @sec-capability).

        notes=[("", "H, high criticality. VL, very low criticality. Tool #1, the impact of the attribute on "

The other attributes of the drug substance register are not measured across the step. Afucosylation, galactosylation and high mannose are formed in the production bioreactor. The membrane retains the antibody whatever its glycoform, so the step is not expected to change their distribution, and they were not measured. Host cell protein and leached Protein A are cleared by the chromatography steps before this one, and PCMP-001 Table 7.1 credits UF/DF with no clearance of either. Fragments form by proteolytic clipping of the antibody in culture and during the harvest hold, and slowly by hydrolysis of the hinge region in solution. Version 1.0 left fragments out of the studies of this step, and PCP-010 keeps that scope. PCMP-001 Table 7.1 assumes that this step does not change fragments, and the drug substance is tested for fragments at release. Viral clearance is credited to low-pH viral inactivation, anion exchange and virus filtration and is not measured here.

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection {#sec-risk}

RA-001 ranked every process parameter of the drug substance process for its potential impact on the CQAs and on process performance, and for its potential to interact with other parameters [@ichq9]. Parameters ranked high, or with a likely interaction, were assigned to multivariate study. Parameters ranked lower, whose range could be supported one factor at a time, were assigned to univariate study (PCMP-001 §4). All `{python} w(N_P)` parameters of UF/DF were assigned to univariate study, and no designed experiment was planned for the step.

Two of the parameters act through the same layer. A higher final DS concentration raises the viscosity of the retentate and, through the bulk concentration, lowers the flux. It therefore sets the flux limit, and with it the TMP at which the polarization layer begins to limit the flux. The effect of TMP may then depend on the final DS concentration. A study that varies one factor at a time cannot resolve such an interaction. It bounds the effect of each parameter at the edge of its range studied, with the others at their set-points (@sec-pars). PCP-010 §4.3 keeps a rule of Version 1.0 for this case. Where a measured attribute approaches its criterion at an edge, the study should be extended to the combination of edges before a range is claimed.

# Materials and methods {#sec-mm}

## Scale-down model and its qualification {#sec-sdm}

The bench-scale model holds the crossflow and the membrane loading at their commercial values, both scaled by membrane area (PCMP-001 §5). The membrane chemistry, the nominal molecular weight cut-off and the feed channel geometry are those of the commercial skid. The TMP, the number of diavolumes and the final concentration do not depend on scale and were set at the values under study. One quantity cannot be matched, the share of the batch held up in the system. With the crossflow and the membrane loading matched per unit area, the antibody passes through the pump as often at bench scale as at commercial scale. The bench skid, however, holds a larger share of its batch in its recirculation loop and has a larger ratio of surface to volume. More antibody is therefore lost to hold-up, and more of it meets surfaces and air-liquid interfaces per gram processed. A slightly lower step yield and slightly more aggregate were expected at bench scale.

The qualification study `{python} SDM_ID` ran from `{python} SDM_START` to `{python} SDM_END` on the skid `{python} SDM_EQ`, under SOP-1001. It compared `{python} w(N_SD)` runs of the model at the set-point condition with `{python} w(N_M)` batches at manufacturing scale. The outputs compared were the step yield, the aggregate content of the final retentate, the final concentration achieved and the permeate flux at the set-point TMP of `{python} sp_s("tmp")`. @tbl-sdm-runs gives the individual runs. The record does not name the manufacturing-scale batches, which PCP-010 §5.1 asks this report to do. The scale-down runs were complete on `{python} SDM_END`, before the first characterization run of the step on `{python} UNI_START`, as PCMP-001 §7.1 requires. The record does not give the date on which the offsets were calculated.

Under PCMP-001 §7.1 the offset of an output is the mean of the scale-down runs at set-point minus the mean of the manufacturing-scale batches, with its two-sided `{python} OFF_CI` % confidence interval. @tbl-sdm-offsets gives the four offsets. The bench skid gave a mean aggregate `{python} fx(OFF[AG]["offset"])` percentage points higher and a mean step yield `{python} fx(-100 * OFF["step_yield"]["offset"], 1)` percentage points lower than manufacturing scale. Both differences are in the direction that the larger hold-up predicts. The interval of each includes zero, and so do the intervals of the final concentration and the permeate flux.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.sdm_offsets([UO]).show()
```

Of the four outputs only aggregate carries a criterion at this step. The offsets of the step yield, the final concentration and the permeate flux are recorded, and no conclusion depends on them (PCMP-001 §7.1). The qualification compared the aggregate content of the final retentate and not the change in aggregate across the step that PCP-010 Table 5.1 names, because the record holds no aggregate result for the load (@sec-sampling). The aggregate offset is therefore subtracted directly from each aggregate result of the final retentate. Every judgement of aggregate against its criterion in this report is stated at manufacturing scale.

PCMP-001 §7.1 decides whether a model is qualified for an output on the response-surface model of the step. This step has none, so @tbl-sdm-offsets marks the qualification under PCMP-001 §7.1 as not applicable, and PCP-010 §7.1 sets no rule for it. This report therefore takes as the conclusion over the NOR whether every individual aggregate result at a level inside the NOR meets the criterion at manufacturing scale. It draws that conclusion with the offset at its estimate and at either end of its interval, as PCMP-001 §7.1 does with a model. All `{python} N_IN_NOR` aggregate results inside the NOR met the criterion in all three cases, so the model is qualified for aggregate. The highest of them was `{python} fx(AGG_NOR_WORST)` % HMW, with the offset at the end of its interval that is least favourable to the criterion.

`{python} UNI2_ID` ran on the second skid `{python} UNI2_EQ` and not on `{python} SDM_EQ`, where the offsets were estimated. Applying the offsets to its results assumes that the two skids give the same result at the set-point condition, and no qualification run compared them. As measured, the `{python} w(N_SP2)` set-point runs of `{python} UNI2_ID` gave a mean aggregate of `{python} fx(AGG_SP2_MEAN)` %, against `{python} fx(AGG_SDM_MEAN)` % for the scale-down runs of `{python} SDM_ID` and `{python} fx(AGG_MFG_MEAN)` % for the manufacturing-scale batches. No conclusion of this report depends on that difference, because the highest aggregate result of `{python} UNI2_ID` lies `{python} fx(AGG_MARGIN)` percentage points below the criterion (@sec-criteria).

The acidic charge variants and the residual process buffer were not compared at both scales. Their offsets are unknown, not zero, and both are judged as measured (PCMP-001 §7.1). For the acidic charge variants this rests on the kinetics of deamidation, which depend on the pH and the temperature of the solution and on the time spent in it, and not on the scale of the skid. At the same TMP and crossflow the flux is the same at both scales, so a run of the model lasts as long as the commercial step at the same settings (PCP-010 §5.1). For the buffer exchange it rests on the passage of the buffer species through the membrane, which depends on the number of diavolumes and on the membrane and not on scale.

## Operation {#sec-operation}

The step receives the filtrate pool of the small virus retentive filtration step. Under SOP-2013 the pool is concentrated by ultrafiltration, diafiltered at constant volume against formulation buffer for the number of diavolumes of the run, concentrated a second time to the final target and recovered with a buffer flush. At the set-point condition the step runs `{python} sp_s("diavolumes")` at a TMP of `{python} sp_s("tmp")` to a final concentration of `{python} sp_s("final_conc")`. The composition of the formulation buffer is fixed by the drug product program and was a constant of the studies. PCP-010 §5.2 loads every run from a single pool of the virus filtration step, so that the variability of the load does not confound the comparison between levels, and §12 of the plan gives a bridging rule if one pool is not sufficient. The record of `{python} UNI2_ID` does not identify the load pool of its runs, so whether one pool served the whole study cannot be confirmed from it.

## Analytical methods {#sec-methods}

The procedures and validated methods are listed in @tbl-sops. Aggregate is measured by size exclusion chromatography (SEC) under AMV-3011 and reported as the percentage of high molecular weight species (HMW). The acidic charge variants are measured by imaged capillary isoelectric focusing (icIEF) under AMV-3013 and reported as the percentage of acidic species. Protein concentration is measured by ultraviolet absorbance (A280) under AMV-3019, and the final concentration and the step yield rest on that measurement. PCP-010 follows the buffer exchange by the conductivity and the pH of the retentate, which are in-process readings of the skid instrumentation and not validated assays. The record of `{python} UNI2_ID` gives one result of the buffer exchange per run, the residual process buffer as a percentage of the process buffer, and no pH reading (@sec-sampling).

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.sop_references(sops=UFDF_SOP_REFS, amvs=UFDF_AMV_REFS).show()
```

The studies of this step do not measure fragments, a scope that PCP-010 keeps from Version 1.0. The analytical method decision AMD-001 of `{python} AMD["date"]` set non-reduced CE-SDS (nrCE-SDS) as the method for fragments at every step, and it therefore changes no result of this report. Aggregate stays with SEC, where the interference that led to AMD-001 does not apply (PCMP-001 §7.8). @tbl-methods-by-study lists the methods for size variants by designed study, and this step has no designed study to list. Aggregate is measured by SEC in both studies of the step (PCP-010 §5.3).

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.methods_by_study([UO]).show()
```

The aggregate content of A-Mab drug substance is low, and a change across this step may be of the size of the repeatability of SEC. PCP-010 §5.3 keeps the rules of Version 1.0 for such small changes. A measured change is judged against the pure error of the study and not against the nominal precision of the method. Noise near the low end of the method range is attributed to the assay unless the change measured across the range is larger than the pure error. @sec-stats states how this rule and the slope test were applied together.

## Sampling plan {#sec-sampling}

@tbl-sampling compares the samples that PCP-010 Table 5.2 planned with the results that the record of `{python} UNI2_ID` holds. The criteria for aggregate and the acidic charge variants apply to the final retentate, and the record holds both results for every run, together with the final concentration and the step yield. It holds one result of the residual process buffer per run. It holds no result for the load pool, the pre-diafiltration retentate or the permeate, and no pH reading. Without a load result the change in aggregate and in the acidic charge variants across the step cannot be calculated. ## Statistical methods {#sec-stats}

For each parameter and each output, the individual results were regressed on the setting of the parameter over the range studied, and the slope was tested against zero at α = `{python} fg(ALPHA)` (PCP-010 §5.5, PCMP-001 §6.2). Each series has `{python} N_SER` runs, so each slope has `{python} SLDF` degrees of freedom. An attribute is called affected by a parameter when its slope is significant at that level. The change across the range studied is the slope times the width of the range. It is reported with its 95 % confidence interval beside the p-value, so that statistical and practical significance are read apart. The criterion, and not the p-value, decides whether a range is acceptable. No response-surface model was fitted, because the study has no factorial structure and no interaction can be estimated from it. The model-adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2 apply to response-surface models and do not apply here.

The duplicate runs at each level give the pure error of the study, the combined variability of the process and the assay, as a pooled standard deviation with `{python} PE_DF` degrees of freedom for each output. PCP-010 §5.3 leaves to this report how its rule for small changes and the slope test are applied together. This report applies both to aggregate, the attribute whose changes the rule concerns. The slope test decides whether aggregate is affected, and the change across the range is compared with the pure error. For aggregate the two agreed for every parameter (@sec-aggregate). The acidic charge variants lie near `{python} fx(AC_MEAN, 0)` %, against a limit of quantitation of `{python} fg(ICIEF_LOQ)` % for icIEF. The rule for the low end of the method range therefore does not apply to them, and the slope test alone decides.

The buffer exchange was analysed by fitting the exponential decay that the mechanism predicts (@sec-prior), as the natural logarithm of the residual process buffer regressed on the number of diavolumes. PCP-010 §5.5 plans that fit on the conductivity series of each run. The record holds no such series, so the fit was made across the runs of the diavolume series, on one result per run. Complete passage of the buffer species through the membrane gives a slope of −1 on that scale.

Each attribute result was judged on its own against its criterion, as PCMP-001 §6.2 requires for a quality attribute and PCP-010 §7.2 states for this step. Aggregate was judged at manufacturing scale and the acidic charge variants as measured (@sec-sdm). The PAR of a parameter is the contiguous span of levels around the set-point over which every attribute result met its criterion, with the other parameters at their set-points (PCP-010 §8).

The record of `{python} UNI2_ID` does not give the order in which its runs were made. The randomized order that PCP-010 §6.2 requires therefore cannot be confirmed from it, and a drift over the course of the study could not be separated from a slope.

The capability of the drug substance comes from the integrated process model of PCMP-001 §6.5. The model runs `{python} N_MC_S` simulated batches through every step. Each process parameter is drawn from a normal distribution centred on its set-point, with a standard deviation of one sixth of the width of its NOR, and the model includes the effects of the UF/DF parameters on aggregate. Cpk is judged against the target and the minimum of PCMP-001 §7.9.

# Study design {#sec-design}

## Factors, ranges and the knowledge space {#sec-factors}

@tbl-factors gives the parameters with their set-points, NORs, ranges studied and the levels of `{python} UNI2_ID`. Each range studied extends beyond the NOR at one end or at both, and it is the knowledge space within which a PAR can be claimed.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_fa = pd.DataFrame([[NAME[k], UNIT[k], fg(SP[k]), f"{fg(NOR[k][0])}–{fg(NOR[k][1])}",
                     f"{fg(RNG[k][0])}–{fg(RNG[k][1])}",
                     ", ".join(fg(v) for v in sorted(U.loc[U["parameter"] == k, "value"].unique()))]
                    for k in PK],
                   columns=["Parameter", "Unit", "Set-point", "NOR", "Range\nstudied", f"Levels of\n{UNI2_ID}"])
T.frame(_fa, "Parameters of the step: set-points, normal operating ranges, ranges studied and the levels "
             "of the univariate study.", "tbl-factors",
        align=["P{4.2cm}", "l", "r", "l", "l", "P{4.0cm}"], size="footnotesize").show()
```

The `{python} nm["diavolumes"]` was studied over `{python} rng_s("diavolumes")` against a NOR of `{python} nor_s("diavolumes")`. The range extends above the NOR because more diavolumes mean more time on the skid and more passes through the pump. Its lower edge is the lower edge of the NOR, the lowest count that the commercial step runs, and the study does not go below it. TMP was studied over `{python} rng_s("tmp")` against a NOR of `{python} nor_s("tmp")`. The range extends above the NOR because pressure above the flux limit compacts the polarization layer without raising throughput. Its lower edge is also the lower edge of the NOR. A lower TMP would lengthen the operation, and the study does not characterize that side. The `{python} nm["final_conc"]` was studied over `{python} rng_s("final_conc")` against a NOR of `{python} nor_s("final_conc")`, on both sides. Above the target it raises the viscosity and the bulk concentration of the retentate and lowers the flux. Below the target it leaves the drug substance below the concentration that the drug product program expects. No PAR is claimed beyond the range studied (PCMP-001 §7.6).

## Univariate assessment {#sec-univariate}

PCP-010 §6.2 planned the study `{python} UNI_ID`. Each parameter was to be run at the two edges of its range studied and at its set-point, with the other two at their set-points. The set-point condition was shared by the series and replicated, and the order of execution was to be randomized across the study. `{python} UNI_ID` ran from `{python} UNI_START` to `{python} UNI_END` on `{python} UNI_EQ`. The record holds no result of it for any parameter effect, and Version 1.0 narrated its outcome without one.

`{python} UNI2_ID` was made from `{python} UNI2_START` to `{python} UNI2_END`, during the re-analysis and after INV-001 closed on `{python} INV["closed"]`. Its purpose was to give the parameters the recorded results that Version 1.0 lacked. Each parameter was run at `{python} w(N_LEV)` levels, in duplicate, with the other two at their set-points. The low and high levels are the edges of the range studied, and the two intermediate levels lie halfway between the set-point and each edge (@tbl-factors). The study has `{python} N_RUNS2` runs, `{python} w(N_SP2)` of them at the set-point condition. It ran on `{python} UNI2_EQ`, a second UF/DF TFF skid, which was in calibration at execution, with its next calibration due on `{python} CALDUE[UNI2_EQ]`. The windows of `{python} SDM_ID` and `{python} UNI_ID` closed before the next calibration of `{python} SDM_EQ`, which was due on `{python} CALDUE[SDM_EQ]`.

`{python} UNI2_ID` is not a designed experiment. No run combines the levels of two parameters, and no model with more than one parameter is fitted to it. It differs from the plan in its levels, its replicates and its skid, and it is recorded as the discrepancy `{python} PD1` (@sec-discrepancies). It answers the absence of results in Version 1.0. No result for a parameter effect existed when it was made, so none of its conclusions rests on runs added after a result was known.

# Results {#sec-results}

@tbl-repro gives the pure error of each output and the results of the `{python} w(N_SP2)` set-point runs, `{python} w(N_REP)` in each series. The pure error of aggregate was `{python} fx(PE[AG][0], 3)` percentage points and that of the acidic charge variants `{python} fx(PE[AC][0])` percentage points. The pure error of the step yield was `{python} fx(PE["yield_pct"][0], 1)` percentage points, and that of the final concentration `{python} fx(PE["ds_concentration_g_per_l"][0])` g/L. The set-point runs of the `{python} w(N_P)` series gave a mean aggregate of `{python} fx(AGG_SP2_MEAN)` % with a standard deviation of `{python} fx(SP2[AG].std(ddof=1), 3)` percentage points.

## Effects of the parameters {#sec-effects}

@tbl-slopes gives, for each parameter and output, the change across the range studied that the slope predicts, its 95 % confidence interval and the p-value of the slope. Of the `{python} N_SLOPES` slopes, `{python} w(N_SIG)` were significant at α = `{python} fg(ALPHA)`. The `{python} nm["diavolumes"]` affected the residual process buffer. TMP and the final DS concentration affected aggregate, and the final DS concentration affected the final concentration achieved, which is its own setting. No slope of the acidic charge variants or of the step yield was significant, and neither TMP nor the final DS concentration had a significant slope on the residual process buffer.

## Aggregate {#sec-aggregate}

Every aggregate result met the criterion of `{python} CRIT_AG` at manufacturing scale, also with the offset at the end of its interval that is least favourable to the criterion. The highest result was `{python} fx(AGG_MAX)` % HMW, `{python} where(AGG_MAX_K, AGG_MAX_V)`, and it lay `{python} fx(AGG_MARGIN)` percentage points below the criterion. @fig-agg-acidic shows the individual results against each parameter.

Aggregate rose with the final DS concentration. Across the range studied of `{python} rng_s("final_conc")` the slope predicts a rise of `{python} fx(sC["ch"])` percentage points (95 % confidence interval `{python} fx(sC["ch_lo"])` to `{python} fx(sC["ch_hi"])`, `{python} pe(sC["p"])`), and across the NOR a rise of `{python} fx(CH_C_NOR)`. Aggregate also rose with TMP, by `{python} fx(sT["ch"])` percentage points across `{python} rng_s("tmp")` (95 % confidence interval `{python} fx(sT["ch_lo"])` to `{python} fx(sT["ch_hi"])`, `{python} pe(sT["p"])`) and by `{python} fx(CH_T_NOR)` across the NOR. Both changes across the range are larger than the pure error of `{python} fx(PE[AG][0], 3)` percentage points, so the rule of PCP-010 §5.3 attributes neither to the assay. Both agree in direction with the expectation of @sec-prior. The larger change, for the final DS concentration, is `{python} fx(SHARE_C, 0)` % of the margin between the highest result and the criterion. This report judges both changes small against the criterion. No plan sets a threshold for that judgement, and @sec-classification uses it.

No effect of the `{python} nm["diavolumes"]` on aggregate was detected (`{python} pe(sDV["p"])`). The 95 % confidence interval of the change across `{python} rng_s("diavolumes")` runs from `{python} fx(sDV["ch_lo"])` to `{python} fx(sDV["ch_hi"])` percentage points. More diavolumes add passes through the pump, and @sec-prior expected aggregate to rise with them. The data do not show that rise at the precision of the study, and an effect within the interval cannot be excluded.
