## Acidic charge variants {#sec-acidic}

Every result of the acidic charge variants lay within the criterion of `{python} CRIT_AC`, at both ends. The lowest result was `{python} fx(AC_MIN, 1)` %, `{python} where(AC_MIN_K, AC_MIN_V)`, `{python} fx(AC_MARGIN_LO, 1)` percentage points above the lower limit. The highest was `{python} fx(AC_MAX, 1)` %, `{python} fx(AC_MARGIN_HI, 1)` percentage points below the upper limit. No slope was significant (`{python} pe(SL[("diavolumes", AC)]["p"])`, `{python} pe(SL[("tmp", AC)]["p"])` and `{python} pe(SL[("final_conc", AC)]["p"])` for the `{python} nm["diavolumes"]`, TMP and the final DS concentration). The 95 % confidence intervals of the change across the range studied run from `{python} fx(SL[("diavolumes", AC)]["ch_lo"], 1)` to `{python} fx(SL[("diavolumes", AC)]["ch_hi"], 1)`, from `{python} fx(SL[("tmp", AC)]["ch_lo"], 1)` to `{python} fx(SL[("tmp", AC)]["ch_hi"], 1)` and from `{python} fx(SL[("final_conc", AC)]["ch_lo"], 1)` to `{python} fx(SL[("final_conc", AC)]["ch_hi"], 1)` percentage points, in the same order. A change of up to `{python} fx(AC_CH_BOUND, 1)` percentage points across a range therefore cannot be excluded. @sec-prior expected a rise with the number of diavolumes and the final DS concentration and a fall with TMP, through the time in solution. The study does not show any of these directions at its precision.

The level of the acidic charge variants is set upstream. It arrives with the load from the virus filtration step and is formed first in the production bioreactor, whose report PCR-003 characterizes it. Without a load result the study cannot say how much deamidation the step adds at the set-point condition (@sec-sampling).

## Buffer exchange {#sec-buffer}

The residual process buffer fell exponentially with the number of diavolumes (@fig-buffer). The slope of its natural logarithm on the number of diavolumes was `{python} fx(RB_B, 3)` (95 % confidence interval `{python} fx(RB_LO, 3)` to `{python} fx(RB_HI, 3)`, R² = `{python} fx(RB_R2, 3)`). The interval includes −1, the slope that complete passage of the buffer species through the membrane gives. Each diavolume removed `{python} fx(RB_REMOVED, 0)` % of the process buffer that remained, and the residual fell by a factor of `{python} fx(RB_FOLD)` per diavolume. At the set-point of `{python} sp_s("diavolumes")` the mean residual was `{python} fx(RB_SP["mean"], 3)` % of the process buffer. At the lower edge of the NOR, `{python} u_("diavolumes", NOR["diavolumes"][0])`, the two results were `{python} fx(RB_NORLO["min"], 3)` and `{python} fx(RB_NORLO["max"], 3)` %. At the top of the range studied, `{python} u_("diavolumes", RNG["diavolumes"][1])`, neither result exceeded `{python} fx(RB_TOP["max"], 4)` %. The residual process buffer had no significant slope on TMP (`{python} pe(SL[("tmp", "residual_buffer_pct")]["p"])`) or on the final DS concentration (`{python} pe(SL[("final_conc", "residual_buffer_pct")]["p"])`), as a wash-out that depends on the number of diavolumes alone would predict.

```{python}
#| label: fig-buffer
#| fig-cap: "Residual process buffer in the final retentate against the number of diavolumes, S-UFDF-UNI2, on a logarithmic scale. Each point is one run. The grey band is the NOR, and the line is the exponential fall fitted to the runs of the series."
#| fig-width: 5.4
#| fig-height: 3.4
_fig, a = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.4, 3.4))
a.axvspan(NOR["diavolumes"][0], NOR["diavolumes"][1], color="0.9", lw=0, zorder=0)
a.semilogy(G["value"], G["residual_buffer_pct"], "o", ms=5, color="#1f5f8b", zorder=3)
_xs = np.linspace(RNG["diavolumes"][0], RNG["diavolumes"][1], 50)
a.semilogy(_xs, np.exp(RB_IC + RB_B * _xs), "-", color="#b5562b", lw=1.4, zorder=2)
a.set_xlabel(f"{NAME['diavolumes']} ({UNIT['diavolumes']})", fontsize=9)
a.set_ylabel("Residual process buffer (%)", fontsize=9)
a.tick_params(labelsize=8)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The two results at each level of the diavolume series lay wholly above both results at the next level, at every step from `{python} u_("diavolumes", RNG["diavolumes"][0])` to `{python} u_("diavolumes", RNG["diavolumes"][1])`. The residual process buffer therefore changed measurably with each further diavolume across the whole range studied, and it reached no plateau within it.

PCP-010 §7.2 accepts the buffer exchange when the conductivity and the pH of the retentate have reached the plateau of the formulation buffer at or below the lower edge of the NOR, `{python} u_("diavolumes", NOR["diavolumes"][0])`. PCP-010 §5.5 places the plateau at the number of diavolumes after which the following diavolume makes no further measurable change. Version 1.0 set no analysis for the pH and no numerical tolerance for the plateau, and PCP-010 leaves both to this report. The record holds no pH reading, so the pH part of the criterion cannot be judged. This report applies the plateau as PCP-010 §5.5 defines it. It sets no numerical tolerance of its own after the results, because a tolerance chosen with the data known would decide the criterion. On that definition the residual process buffer shows no plateau at or below `{python} u_("diavolumes", NOR["diavolumes"][0])`. The buffer-exchange criterion of PCP-010 §7.2 is therefore not met.

Objective (iii) is met only in part. The study establishes how much process buffer remains after each number of diavolumes, but not the plateau that the plan required. At the lower edge of the NOR the residual process buffer is at most `{python} fx(RB_NORLO["max"], 3)` % of the process buffer. Whether that residual is acceptable depends on what the formulation tolerates, and the record holds no limit for it. This report makes no claim that the buffer exchange is complete at `{python} u_("diavolumes", NOR["diavolumes"][0])`.

## Step yield and final concentration {#sec-yield}

The step yield ranged from `{python} fx(Y_MIN, 1)` to `{python} fx(Y_MAX, 1)` %, with a mean of `{python} fx(Y_MEAN, 1)` %. No slope of the step yield was significant. The 95 % confidence intervals of its change across the range studied run from `{python} fx(SL[("diavolumes", "yield_pct")]["ch_lo"], 1)` to `{python} fx(SL[("diavolumes", "yield_pct")]["ch_hi"], 1)` percentage points for the `{python} nm["diavolumes"]`, from `{python} fx(SL[("tmp", "yield_pct")]["ch_lo"], 1)` to `{python} fx(SL[("tmp", "yield_pct")]["ch_hi"], 1)` for TMP and from `{python} fx(SL[("final_conc", "yield_pct")]["ch_lo"], 1)` to `{python} fx(SL[("final_conc", "yield_pct")]["ch_hi"], 1)` for the final DS concentration. The step yield has no criterion and is reported for information.

The final concentration followed its setting in the series of the final DS concentration, with a slope of `{python} fx(sFC["slope"], 3)` (95 % confidence interval `{python} fx(sFC["lo"], 3)` to `{python} fx(sFC["hi"], 3)`). Each result lay within `{python} fx(FC_DIFF_MAX, 1)` g/L of its setting. In the other two series, run at the target of `{python} sp_s("final_conc")`, the final concentration ranged from `{python} fx(FC_OTH.min(), 1)` to `{python} fx(FC_OTH.max(), 1)` g/L, inside the NOR of `{python} nor_s("final_conc")`. The pure error of the final concentration, `{python} fx(PE["ds_concentration_g_per_l"][0])` g/L, compares with a precision of the A280 method of `{python} fg(A280_PREC)` %, which is `{python} fx(A280_SD_AT_TARGET, 1)` g/L at the target.

## Mechanistic interpretation {#sec-mechanism}

The rise of aggregate with the final DS concentration and with TMP is consistent with aggregate forming in the polarization layer at the membrane wall. Both parameters raise the antibody concentration there. The final DS concentration raises it through the bulk concentration at the end of the operation. Below the flux limit TMP raises it by driving more permeate through the membrane, and above the limit it compacts the layer at the wall. The study did not measure the flux across the TMP range, so it cannot say on which side of the flux limit the set-point lies. Within the NOR the two effects amount to `{python} fx(CH_C_NOR)` and `{python} fx(CH_T_NOR)` percentage points.

No effect of the number of diavolumes on aggregate was detected, although more diavolumes add passes through the pump. Diafiltration is made before the second concentration, at a lower antibody concentration than the final one. If aggregate forms mainly where the concentration at the wall is highest, extra diavolumes at that lower concentration would add little. This is an expectation that the study did not test.

The acidic charge variants did not change detectably over the ranges studied, although each parameter changes the time the antibody spends in solution. The record does not give the duration of the runs, so the study cannot relate the acidic charge variants to the time in solution.

The fall of the residual process buffer by a factor of `{python} fx(RB_FOLD)` for each diavolume is consistent with free passage of the buffer species through the membrane, which diafiltration at constant volume relies on. The study did not measure the pH or the excipient levels of the final retentate. It therefore gives no evidence on the Donnan and volume-exclusion effects that can leave them off the values of the buffer at high concentration.

For operation, the final DS concentration and TMP are the parameters through which the step changes aggregate, and their control within the NORs bounds that change by the values above. The number of diavolumes sets the residual process buffer.

# Design space {#sec-design-space}

No design space is defined for UF/DF. A design space is a multivariate region [@ichq8]. A study that varies one parameter at a time cannot define one, because it gives no result where two parameters are away from their set-points at the same time. The step is described instead by the univariate PAR of each parameter (@sec-pars), with the NOR inside the PAR and the PAR equal to the range studied. These data support the movement of one parameter within its PAR, with the others at their set-points. They support the movement of two parameters away from their set-points at the same time only as far as the bound on an interaction in @sec-par-table goes. Operation within the NORs is routine. An excursion outside a NOR in manufacture is dispositioned against the PAR (PCP-010 §8). A planned move of an operating range is a change, and it is assessed under change management before it is made [@ichq10].

# Proven acceptable ranges {#sec-pars}

## Acceptance basis {#sec-basis-par}

No step follows UF/DF, so PCMP-001 Table 7.1 defines no IAC for it, and the drug substance criteria apply directly (PCMP-001 §7.6). Aggregate must not exceed `{python} fg(AG_HI)` % HMW, and the acidic charge variants must lie between `{python} fg(AC_LO)` and `{python} fg(AC_HI)` %. Both criteria come from the drug substance CQA register (PCMP-001 §3), and no result of these studies enters them.

The derivation of the criteria upstream of this step assumes that no step after cation exchange changes aggregate, and that no step after low-pH viral inactivation changes the acidic charge variants (PCMP-001 Table 7.1). The cation exchange pool therefore carries the drug substance criterion for aggregate itself. This study shows that two parameters of UF/DF change aggregate. Within the NORs they raise it by up to `{python} fx(ADD_NOR)` percentage points above its level at the set-point, at the corner of `{python} u_("final_conc", NOR["final_conc"][1])` and `{python} u_("tmp", NOR["tmp"][1])`, on the sum of the two slopes. The step therefore does not leave aggregate unchanged across its NOR, as PCMP-001 Table 7.1 assumes, and the cation exchange criterion makes no allowance for that increase. The study measured no change across the step at the set-point condition, because the record holds no load result. No criterion was changed. PCMP-001 §7.5 verifies a platform worst case on the response-surface model of the step that performs it, and PCP-010 §7.2 plans no verification at this step. The integrated process model includes the effect and puts no simulated drug substance batch above the aggregate criterion (@sec-capability). For the acidic charge variants no slope was significant, and the change across the step was not measured either.

## Results against the criteria {#sec-criteria}

@tbl-levels gives, for each level of each parameter, the highest aggregate result at manufacturing scale and the range of the acidic charge variants. Every attribute result of every level met its criterion, so every level is acceptable under the first decision rule of PCP-010 §7.3. The second rule passes a parameter over its range when every level is acceptable and the change measured across the range is small against the criterion. PCP-010 leaves the threshold for a small change to this report, and no plan sets one. This report sets no threshold after the results. It gives the changes (@tbl-slopes) and the margins (@tbl-levels), and it judges every change small against its criterion. The largest significant change of an attribute across a range, `{python} fx(sC["ch"])` percentage points of aggregate for the final DS concentration, is `{python} fx(SHARE_C_CRIT, 1)` % of the criterion of `{python} fg(AG_HI)` % HMW. The changes of the acidic charge variants are not significant. The largest of them, `{python} fx(AC_CH_MAX, 1)` percentage points across the range of the `{python} nm[AC_CH_MAX_K]`, is smaller than the margin of `{python} fx(AC_MARGIN_LO, 1)` percentage points between the lowest result and the lower limit. No level failed, so the rules for a failing level were not used, and the record shows no repeated run.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_lv = []
for k in PK:
    _g = U[U["parameter"] == k]
    for lvl in LEVELS:
        _h = _g[_g["level"] == lvl]
        _v = float(_h["value"].iloc[0])
        _ok = bool((_h["agg_mfg"] <= AG_HI).all() and _h[AC].between(AC_LO, AC_HI).all())
        _lv.append([f"{NAME[k]} ({UNIT[k]})", Cap(lvl), fg(_v),
                    "Yes" if NOR[k][0] <= _v <= NOR[k][1] else "No",
                    fx(_h["agg_mfg"].max(), 2),
                    f"{fx(_h[AC].min(), 1)}–{fx(_h[AC].max(), 1)}", "Yes" if _ok else "No"])
_lv = pd.DataFrame(_lv, columns=["Parameter", "Level", "Setting", "Inside\nthe NOR",
                                 "Aggregates, HMW,\nhighest result (%)", "Acidic variants,\nlowest–highest (%)",
                                 "Both criteria\nmet"])
T.frame(_lv, f"Results of each level against the criteria, {UNI2_ID}.", "tbl-levels", merge=["Parameter"],
        align=["P{3.2cm}", "l", "r", "c", "r", "r", "c"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", f"The criteria are {CRIT_AG} for aggregate and {CRIT_AC} for the acidic variants. Aggregate "
                    "at manufacturing scale, the scale-down result minus the aggregate offset. Acidic variants as "
                    f"measured. Each level has {N_REP} runs.")]).show()
```

## Proven acceptable ranges of the parameters {#sec-par-table}

@tbl-pars gives the PAR of each parameter. Each PAR is the range studied and reaches both edges of it, so no claim is made beyond the range studied (PCMP-001 §7.6). Each PAR rests on aggregate and the acidic charge variants, the attributes the study measured, and on no other attribute. The NOR lies inside each PAR. For the final DS concentration the PAR extends `{python} u_("final_conc", MARG["final_conc"][0])` beyond the NOR at each end. For the `{python} nm["diavolumes"]` and TMP it extends beyond the NOR at the upper end only, by `{python} u_("diavolumes", MARG["diavolumes"][1])` and `{python} u_("tmp", MARG["tmp"][1])`, and its lower edge is the lower edge of the NOR.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_pa = pd.DataFrame([[NAME[k], nor_s(k), f"{fg(PARS[k][0])}–{fg(PARS[k][1])} {UNIT[k]}",
                     u_(k, MARG[k][0]), u_(k, MARG[k][1])] for k in PK],
                   columns=["Parameter", "NOR", "PAR", "PAR beyond\nthe NOR, low", "PAR beyond\nthe NOR, high"])
T.frame(_pa, "Proven acceptable ranges of the parameters, with the other parameters at their set-points. "
             "Each PAR reaches both edges of the range studied.",
        "tbl-pars", align=["P{4.2cm}", "l", "l", "r", "r"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "Each PAR rests on aggregate and the acidic charge variants, the attributes measured in the "
                    "final retentate.")]).show()
```

Three limitations apply to these PARs, as PCP-010 §8 states them.

1. Each PAR holds with the other parameters at their set-points. It does not describe the step when two parameters sit at their range edges at the same time.
2. The NOR-propagated analysis of PCMP-001 §6.4 needs a fitted multivariate model and was not performed. For a parameter studied one factor at a time the range rests on its own data instead (PCMP-001 §4).
3. A PAR cannot be wider than the range studied.

PCP-010 §4.3 extends a study to the combination of edges where a measured attribute approaches its criterion at an edge, and it leaves the threshold for "approaches" to this report. This report sets no numerical threshold after the results. At every edge the highest aggregate result lay at least `{python} fx(EDGE_AG_MARGIN)` percentage points below its criterion, and the acidic charge variants lay at least `{python} fx(EDGE_AC_MARGIN, 1)` percentage points inside theirs. This report judges that no attribute approached its criterion at an edge. No run combined the edges of two parameters.

The interaction of TMP and the final DS concentration that @sec-risk describes was therefore not measured. Its possible size can be set against the criterion. From the mean of the set-point runs at manufacturing scale, `{python} fx(SP_AGG_MFG)` % HMW, the two slopes give `{python} fx(PRED_RNG)` % HMW at the corner of the ranges studied, `{python} u_("final_conc", RNG["final_conc"][1])` and `{python} u_("tmp", RNG["tmp"][1])`. An interaction would have to add a further `{python} fx(GAP_RNG)` percentage points there, about `{python} fx(RATIO_RNG, 0)` times the two effects together, to bring the mean to the criterion. The study cannot exclude an interaction, and it did not measure one.

# Process capability and robustness {#sec-capability}

UF/DF delivers the drug substance, so this report gives the capability of the drug substance for the attributes that the step can change and for residual DNA. @tbl-capability gives the result of the integrated process model for `{python} N_MC_S` simulated batches, with every process parameter drawn within its NOR (PCMP-001 §6.5). The model includes an effect of the final DS concentration and of TMP on aggregate. The table gives each Cpk against the target of `{python} fx(CPK_TARGET)` and the minimum of `{python} fx(CPK_MIN)` of PCMP-001 §7.9, the count of simulated batches outside the criterion and the tail probability of a normal distribution with the simulated mean and standard deviation.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_crit = cqas_by_keys(["aggregates_hmw", "acidic_variants", "residual_dna"])["Acceptance"].tolist()
_cp = []
for _n, (k, dm, ds) in enumerate([("aggregates_hmw", 2, 3), ("acidic_variants", 1, 2), ("residual_dna", 5, 5)]):
    _c = float(CAPT.loc[k, "Cpk"])
    _cp.append([CAPT.loc[k, "cqa"], _crit[_n], fx(MCS[k][0], dm), fx(MCS[k][1], ds), fx(_c, 2), verdict(_c),
                str(NOOS[k]), "< 0.001" if PPM[k] < 0.001 else fx(PPM[k], 0)])
_cp = pd.DataFrame(_cp, columns=["CQA", "Criterion", "Mean", "SD", "Cpk", "Against PCMP-001 §7.9",
                                 f"Batches outside\n(of {N_MC_S})", "Normal tail\n(per million)"])
T.frame(_cp, "Capability of the drug substance in the integrated process model.", "tbl-capability",
        align=["P{3.2cm}", "P{2.4cm}", "r", "r", "r", "P{2.6cm}", "r", "r"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", f"Mean and SD of the simulated batches. Residual DNA in ng per dose, for a dose of "
                    f"{fg(DOSE_MG)} mg of antibody. Normal tail, the probability beyond the criterion of a normal "
                    "distribution with the simulated mean and SD, two-sided for a two-sided criterion.")]).show()
```

Aggregate has a Cpk of `{python} fx(CPK_AG, 1)`, above the target, and no simulated batch lay outside its criterion. The mean simulated aggregate is `{python} fx(MCS["aggregates_hmw"][0])` % HMW, with a standard deviation of `{python} fx(MCS["aggregates_hmw"][1], 3)` percentage points. A Cpk this large says only that the criterion lies far beyond the simulated batches. Aggregate is therefore judged on the individual results of the study (@sec-criteria) and on the count of simulated batches outside the criterion. With none of `{python} N_MC_S` outside, the one-sided 95 % upper confidence bound of the probability of a batch outside is `{python} fx(P_UB_PCT, 2)` %. That bound covers the sampling of the simulation and not the uncertainty of the integrated process model.

The acidic charge variants have a Cpk of `{python} fx(CPK_AC)`, between the minimum and the target. Under PCMP-001 §7.9 a Cpk between the two values is acceptable, and it is accepted here. The lower end of the criterion, `{python} fg(AC_LO)` %, limits it. Of the `{python} N_MC_S` simulated batches, `{python} w(NOOS["acidic_variants"])` fell outside the criterion, and the normal tail probability is `{python} fx(PPM["acidic_variants"], 0)` per million. No slope of the acidic charge variants on a UF/DF parameter was significant (@sec-acidic), so this step does not drive the capability. The attribute is formed in the production bioreactor, and its report PCR-003 gives the parameters that drive it and the controls that address them.

Residual DNA is judged in ng per dose, the unit of its criterion of `{python} fg(DNA_CRIT)` ng per dose. The dose is A-Mab's `{python} fg(DOSE["mg_per_kg"])` mg/kg [@amab2009, p. 26] for a body weight of `{python} fg(DOSE["body_weight_kg"])` kg. The body weight is an assumption of this campaign, and with it a dose carries `{python} fg(DOSE_MG)` mg of antibody. The simulated drug substance carries a mean of `{python} fx(DNA_MEAN, 5)` ng per dose, or `{python} fx(DNA_PG, 5)` pg per mg of antibody, with a Cpk of `{python} fx(CPK_DNA, 1)`. No simulated batch lay outside the criterion, and the same upper bound of `{python} fx(P_UB_PCT, 2)` % applies. This result rests on the DNA clearance that the integrated process model assigns to each purification step, which is an input from outside the data of this step. The reports of the capture and polishing steps (PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008) give the DNA results of their studies. Residual DNA has no IAC, because the platform history gives no worst-case DNA clearance for the steps after Protein A, so no criterion can be carried back (PCMP-001 §7.3). DNA is controlled by the clearance of the purification steps and not by a release test [@amab2009, p. 47]. No DNA clearance is credited to UF/DF.

The step met both of its criteria at every level of the range studied of every parameter (@sec-criteria).

# Parameter classification {#sec-classification}

The parameters were classified under SOP-4001 by the rules of PCMP-001 §7.7, which follow the decision logic of the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]. A critical process parameter (CPP) has a significant and practically relevant effect on a CQA within the characterized range and a high risk of falling outside its acceptable range in operation. A well-controlled critical process parameter has the same kind of effect but a low risk, because it is readily controlled and its PAR is wide against its NOR. A KPP affects process performance, such as yield or concentration, and has no effect on a CQA within its range. A significant effect that is too small to move the attribute appreciably within the PAR does not by itself make a parameter critical. PCMP-001 and SOP-4001 set no numerical threshold for a small effect or a wide PAR. Each class below is therefore stated with the size of each effect across the PAR and the margin of the PAR to the NOR (PCP-010 §7.4). @tbl-classification summarises the evidence.

```{python}
#| output: asis
def _aff(k):
    _a = [RLAB[r].split(" (")[0] for r in (AG, AC) if (k, r) in SIG]
    return "None detected" if not _a else ", ".join(f"{x} ({pe(SL[(k, AG if x.startswith('Agg') else AC)]['p'])})"
                                                    for x in _a)
_perf = {"diavolumes": "Residual process buffer", "tmp": "Permeate flux, from the mechanism of the step",
         "final_conc": "Final concentration"}
_cl = pd.DataFrame([[NAME[k], _aff(k),
                     f"{fx(SL[(k, AG)]['ch'])} ({fx(SL[(k, AG)]['ch_lo'])} to {fx(SL[(k, AG)]['ch_hi'])})",
                     _perf[k], f"{u_(k, MARG[k][0])} / {u_(k, MARG[k][1])}"] for k in PK],
                   columns=["Parameter", "Attribute affected", "Change of aggregate\nacross the PAR (pp)",
                            "Performance\noutput it sets", "PAR beyond the\nNOR, low / high"])
assert len(set(CLS.values())) == 1
T.frame(_cl, f"Evidence for the classification of the parameters, each classified as a {CLS['tmp']}.",
        "tbl-classification", align=["P{3.0cm}", "P{2.6cm}", "r", "P{3.0cm}", "l"],
        size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "pp, percentage points of HMW. Change, the slope times the width of the PAR, with its 95 % "
                    "confidence interval in brackets.")]).show()
```

- The `{python} nm["diavolumes"]` was classified as a KPP. It sets the completeness of the buffer exchange, and the residual process buffer fell by a factor of `{python} fx(RB_FOLD)` for each diavolume (@sec-buffer). Its slopes on aggregate (`{python} pe(sDV["p"])`) and on the acidic charge variants (`{python} pe(SL[("diavolumes", AC)]["p"])`) were not significant. No effect on either attribute, the two that the study measured, was detected within the range studied, at the precision of the duplicates. Its PAR of `{python} rng_s("diavolumes")` extends `{python} u_("diavolumes", MARG["diavolumes"][1])` above the NOR and not below it.
- TMP was classified as a KPP. Its effect on aggregate was significant (`{python} pe(sT["p"])`) and amounts to `{python} fx(sT["ch"])` percentage points across its PAR of `{python} rng_s("tmp")`, which is `{python} fx(100 * sT["ch"] / AG_HI, 1)` % of the criterion. This report judges that effect too small to move aggregate appreciably within the PAR, so under PCMP-001 §7.7 it does not by itself make TMP critical. TMP drives the permeate flux and so the duration of the operation (@sec-prior). The flux was measured only at the set-point, in `{python} SDM_ID`, and not across the TMP range. The performance effect on which the class rests therefore comes from the mechanism of the step and not from this study. The PAR extends `{python} u_("tmp", MARG["tmp"][1])` above the NOR and not below it.
- The final DS concentration was classified as a KPP. It sets the concentration of the drug substance, which followed it with a slope of `{python} fx(sFC["slope"], 3)` (@sec-yield). Its effect on aggregate was significant (`{python} pe(sC["p"])`) and amounts to `{python} fx(sC["ch"])` percentage points across its PAR of `{python} rng_s("final_conc")`, which is `{python} fx(SHARE_C_CRIT, 1)` % of the criterion. This report judges that effect too small to move aggregate appreciably within the PAR. The PAR extends `{python} u_("final_conc", MARG["final_conc"][0])` beyond the NOR at each end.

The step has no CPP and no well-controlled CPP. Its `{python} w(N_P)` parameters are KPPs, which are controlled within their NORs so that the step performs consistently [@amab2009].

# Contribution to the control strategy {#sec-control}

The control strategy for the drug substance process is consolidated in PCMR-001. This report contributes the following.

1. The NORs of the parameters, `{python} nor_s("diavolumes")`, `{python} nor_s("tmp")` and `{python} nor_s("final_conc")`, lie inside their PARs, which are the ranges studied. The parameters are KPPs. They are controlled within their NORs so that the step delivers the drug substance consistently at its target concentration and in the formulation buffer.
2. The final DS concentration and TMP are the parameters through which the step changes aggregate. Their control within the NORs bounds that change by the values of @sec-basis-par. In the studies TMP was monitored in process and the final concentration was checked by A280, and these two checks detected the study events DEV-010-01 and DEV-010-02 (@sec-events).
3. The number of diavolumes sets the residual process buffer. The buffer-exchange criterion of PCP-010 is not met (@sec-buffer), and the record holds no limit for the residual process buffer that the formulation tolerates. The lower edge of the diavolume NOR, `{python} u_("diavolumes", NOR["diavolumes"][0])`, therefore rests on the measured residual and not on a demonstrated plateau.
4. The membrane chemistry and the membrane supplier are part of the qualified state of the step, and a change to either requires a new risk assessment before these data are applied (PCP-010 §12). The composition of the formulation buffer is fixed by the drug product program, and a change to it would change the target of the buffer exchange.

The attributes that other steps control are named by their reports. The glycan variants and the acidic charge variants are formed in the production bioreactor (PCR-003). Fragments form during the harvest hold (PCR-004) and are tested at release. Host cell protein and residual DNA are cleared by the chromatography steps (PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008), and residual DNA is controlled by clearance and not by a release test. Leached Protein A enters the process at capture (PCR-005) and is cleared by the polishing steps. Viral clearance is credited to low-pH viral inactivation, anion exchange and virus filtration (PCR-006, PCR-008 and PCR-009), and the cumulative claim is consolidated in PCMR-001.

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

The studies show how the `{python} w(N_P)` parameters of UF/DF act on the drug substance within the ranges studied. Two of them, the final DS concentration and TMP, raise aggregate, by amounts that exceed the pure error of the study and that this report judges small against the criterion. The number of diavolumes sets the residual process buffer, which falls by the factor that free passage of the buffer species predicts. No slope of the acidic charge variants was significant. Every result met the drug substance criteria, and each parameter has a PAR equal to its range studied.

Confidence in the scale-down model rests on its offsets. The intervals of all four offsets include zero, and the model is qualified for aggregate under the approach of @sec-sdm. Three points limit that confidence. The offsets were estimated on `{python} SDM_EQ`, while `{python} UNI2_ID` ran on `{python} UNI2_EQ`, and no run compared the two skids. The acidic charge variants and the residual process buffer were not compared at both scales, so their representativeness rests on the kinetics of deamidation and on the passage of the buffer species through the membrane. The record does not name the manufacturing-scale batches. The highest aggregate result lies `{python} fx(AGG_MARGIN)` percentage points below the criterion, so none of these points changes a conclusion about aggregate.

The record of `{python} UNI2_ID` is incomplete against the plan in four respects that bear on its reading. It holds no load result, so the change across the step is unknown and the study measures only how the parameters change the final retentate. It holds no pH reading and no series of readings within a run, so the buffer-exchange criterion could not be applied as the plan states it, and it is not met on the results that exist. It does not give the order of the runs, so a drift over the study cannot be separated from a slope. It does not identify the load pool. @sec-record records the departures from the plan.

The principal scientific limitation is the univariate design. It cannot measure an interaction, and the possible interaction of TMP and the final DS concentration through the polarization layer is the one that matters for aggregate. @sec-par-table sets its possible size against the criterion. Each slope rests on `{python} SLDF` degrees of freedom, so an effect smaller than the confidence intervals of @tbl-slopes may have gone undetected, for the acidic charge variants in particular.

The aggregate effect also bears on the criteria upstream. PCMP-001 Table 7.1 assumes that no step after cation exchange changes aggregate, and this step does change it within its NOR (@sec-basis-par). No criterion was changed, because no verification is planned at a step without a response-surface model. The integrated process model includes the effect and gives drug substance aggregate a Cpk of `{python} fx(CPK_AG, 1)` (@sec-capability).

The ranges and classes of this report are the ones against which the PPQ batches of PTP-001 will be run at the receiving site (PCMP-001 §2).

# Conclusions {#sec-conclusions}

1. The bench-scale TFF model differs from manufacturing scale by offsets whose intervals include zero for all four outputs compared, and it is qualified for aggregate (objective i).
2. Aggregate rises with the final DS concentration and with TMP, by `{python} fx(sC["ch"])` and `{python} fx(sT["ch"])` percentage points across the ranges studied. No effect of the number of diavolumes on aggregate was detected, and no slope of the acidic charge variants was significant (objective ii).
3. The residual process buffer falls by a factor of `{python} fx(RB_FOLD)` for each diavolume and reaches no plateau within the range studied. The buffer-exchange criterion of PCP-010 is not met, and the number of diavolumes at which the retentate reaches the formulation buffer was not established (objective iii).
4. Every result met the drug substance criteria for aggregate and the acidic charge variants. The PARs are `{python} rng_s("diavolumes")`, `{python} rng_s("tmp")` and `{python} rng_s("final_conc")`, each equal to its range studied (objective iv).
5. The `{python} w(N_P)` parameters are KPPs, and the step has no CPP. The drug substance has a Cpk of `{python} fx(CPK_AG, 1)` for aggregate, `{python} fx(CPK_AC)` for the acidic charge variants and `{python} fx(CPK_DNA, 1)` for residual DNA. The tightest, for the acidic charge variants, lies between the minimum and the target of PCMP-001 and is set upstream of this step (objective v).
6. The two study events change no conclusion, and the study `{python} UNI2_ID` is the discrepancy `{python} PD1` from the plan. The results roll up into PCMR-001.

# Study events and discrepancies from the plan {#sec-record}

A process characterization study is not GMP manufacture and raises no deviation. PCP-010 §13 keeps the wording of Version 1.0, which records a departure from the plan during execution as a deviation. This report records two kinds of entry instead. The study events are the events of execution that Version 1.0 recorded, under the numbers that Version 1.0 gave them. The discrepancies from the plan are the departures from PCP-010, both work that the plan did not foresee and requirements of the plan that were not met.

## Study events {#sec-events}

Version 1.0 recorded `{python} w(len(EVS))` study events at this step, which @tbl-events lists.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(dev_register(DOC))
print()
print(": Study events recorded at the step. {#tbl-events}")
```

The record of each event does not name the study or the run in which it occurred. DEV-010-01 names the skid `{python} EV1_EQ`, on which `{python} SDM_ID` and `{python} UNI_ID` ran. No result of `{python} UNI_ID` is in the record, so an event in one of its runs affects no result of this report. The assessments below cover the case in which an event occurred in a run of `{python} SDM_ID`.

### DEV-010-01, transmembrane pressure above the NOR {#sec-dev1}

During concentration the TMP of one run rose to `{python} u_("tmp", dev_010_01_tmp_max_psi)`, above the upper edge of its NOR of `{python} u_("tmp", NOR["tmp"][1])`. In-process TMP monitoring detected the excursion. The investigation attributed it to a transient fouling of the membrane, and the run was retained. The excursion lay within the range studied of `{python} rng_s("tmp")`, over which every aggregate result of `{python} UNI2_ID` met its criterion (@sec-criteria). If the run was one of the scale-down runs of `{python} SDM_ID`, held at that TMP throughout, the upper 95 % confidence limit of the slope of aggregate on TMP puts its effect at no more than `{python} fx(DEV1_EFFECT_HI, 3)` percentage points. It would then have raised the mean of the `{python} w(N_SD)` scale-down runs, and with it the aggregate offset, by at most `{python} fx(DEV1_SHIFT, 3)` percentage points. With the offset lowered by that amount, every aggregate result at manufacturing scale would still meet the criterion.

### DEV-010-02, final concentration below target {#sec-dev2}

The final concentration check of one run measured `{python} u_("final_conc", dev_010_02_conc_pre_g_per_l)` by A280 (`{python} EV2_METHOD`), below the target of `{python} sp_s("final_conc")` and inside the NOR of `{python} nor_s("final_conc")`. The investigation attributed the shortfall to the residual hold-up volume of the skid, the property of the bench skid that @sec-sdm expects to lower its step yield. The run was topped up, as the record states, and retained. The record does not give the concentration after the top-up. The concentration before the top-up lay within the range studied, over which every attribute result of `{python} UNI2_ID` met its criterion. Had the run been one of the scale-down runs of `{python} SDM_ID`, it would enter the offset of the final concentration, which has no criterion at this step, so no conclusion depends on it.

## Discrepancies from the plan {#sec-discrepancies}

@tbl-discrepancies lists the discrepancy from PCP-010 in the register of this report.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(discrepancy_register(DOC))
print()
print(": Discrepancies from the plan PCP-010. {#tbl-discrepancies}")
```

PCP-010 planned the univariate study `{python} UNI_ID` on the skid `{python} SDM_EQ`. Each parameter was to be run at the two edges of its range studied and at its set-point, with a replicated set-point condition shared by the series. `{python} UNI_ID` was run, but Version 1.0 described and narrated it without a result for any parameter effect, and the record holds none. During the re-analysis the further study `{python} UNI2_ID` was made, from `{python} UNI2_START` to `{python} UNI2_END`, to give the parameters recorded results. It ran each parameter at `{python} w(N_LEV)` levels in duplicate, with the others at their set-points, on the second skid `{python} UNI2_EQ`. The plan did not foresee it.

The study changed the basis of the report. Every result, PAR and class of this report rests on `{python} UNI2_ID`. It ran on a skid other than the one on which the offsets were estimated, which @sec-sdm assesses. It was made after INV-001 had closed and after the absence of results in Version 1.0 had been found, but before any result for a parameter effect existed. No conclusion therefore rests on runs added after a result was known.

Departures of `{python} UNI2_ID` from the measurements and analyses of PCP-010 are stated where they bear on a result. They concern the samples of the load, the pre-diafiltration retentate and the permeate, and the pH (@sec-sampling). They also concern the analysis and the criterion of the buffer exchange (@sec-buffer), the order of execution and the load pool (@sec-stats, @sec-operation), and the manufacturing-scale batches of the qualification (@sec-sdm). Where PCP-010 sets no rule, this report states the approach it takes (@sec-sdm, @sec-stats, @sec-criteria, @sec-par-table).

```{python}
    "Aggregates,\nHMW (%)": [fx(v, 2) for v in _a[AG]],
    "Acidic\nvariants (%)": [fx(v, 1) for v in _a[AC]],
    "Residual\nbuffer (%)": [fx(v, 4) for v in _a["residual_buffer_pct"]],
    "Step\nyield (%)": [fx(v, 1) for v in _a["yield_pct"]],
    "Final\nconc. (g/L)": [fx(v, 1) for v in _a["ds_concentration_g_per_l"]]})
T.frame(_ta, f"Results of the univariate study {UNI2_ID}, by parameter and setting.", "tbl-uni2",
        merge=["Parameter", "Setting"],
        align=["P{3.0cm}", "r", "c", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "Run, the replicate at the setting. The other parameters at their set-points. Aggregate as "
                    "measured. Residual buffer, the residual process buffer as a percentage of the process buffer. "
                    "Final conc., the final concentration.")]).show()
```

```{python}
print(appendix_numbering("B"))
```

# Appendix B. Runs of the scale-down qualification {#sec-appB .unnumbered}

@tbl-sdm-runs lists the runs of `{python} SDM_ID` behind the offsets of @tbl-sdm-offsets.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_q = csv("sdm_qualification.csv")
_q = _q[(_q["step"] == UO) & (_q["study"] == SDM_ID)].copy()
_q["__o"] = _q["scale"].map({"scale-down": 0, "manufacturing": 1})
_q = _q.sort_values(["__o", "run"])
_tq = pd.DataFrame({
    "Scale": ["Scale-down model" if s == "scale-down" else "Manufacturing scale" for s in _q["scale"]],
    "Run": [str(int(r)) for r in _q["run"]],
    "Step yield\n(%)": [fx(100 * v, 1) for v in _q["step_yield"]],
    "Aggregates,\nHMW (%)": [fx(v, 2) for v in _q[AG]],
    "Final conc.\n(g/L)": [fx(v, 1) for v in _q["ds_concentration_g_per_l"]],
    "Permeate\nflux (LMH)": [fx(v, 1) for v in _q["flux_lmh"]]})
assert len(_tq) == N_SD + N_M
T.frame(_tq, f"Runs of the scale-down qualification {SDM_ID}, at the set-point condition.", "tbl-sdm-runs",
        merge=["Scale"], align=["P{3.2cm}", "c", "r", "r", "r", "r"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "Final conc., the final concentration achieved. Permeate flux at the set-point TMP. The record "
                    "does not name the manufacturing-scale batches.")]).show()
```
